useCase.name: Let a teacher raise a meeting with a guardian about something they have noticed, proposing the slot themselves
useCase.featureRef: 14.12 Teacher requests a meeting with a guardian

intent.name: teacher.meeting.request.raise
intent.summary: A teacher raises a meeting with a guardian about something they have noticed, proposing the slot themselves. One step, and the reason goes with the slot.
routesHere: raise a meeting with this student's guardian about their work

routesHere.text: is bache ke walidain se mulaqat rakhni hai
routesHere.gloss: I need to arrange a meeting with this child's guardian

routesHere.text: mangal ke teesre period mein bula lo
routesHere.gloss: call them in for Tuesday period 3

routesHere.text: walidain ko wajah ke sath waqt bhej do
routesHere.gloss: send the guardian the reason and a time

request.text: walidain ne khud mulaqat mangi hai
request.gloss: the guardian asked for the meeting themselves

routesElsewhere.note: That is the reverse: the request arrives first and the teacher offers a slot in response (BR-4, UC-14-08 BR-3).

request.text: Coordinator se manzoori le lo
request.gloss: get the coordinator's approval

routesElsewhere.note: No coordinator approval is required for a teacher to raise a request. The coordinator sees what is happening; they do not gate it (BR-11).

request.text: mulaqat parent-teacher meeting mein rakh do
request.gloss: put the meeting into the parent-teacher event

routesElsewhere.note: That is the school-wide meeting day, which books nothing. Families attend during the announced window and see whoever is present (UC-14-11 BR-10), so a concern about one child cannot be parked there.

steps.note: One step, and the guardian is told the reason at the same time as the proposed slot. A family asked to attend without being told why cannot judge whether they can (BR-12).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A student the teacher does not teach is not listed, no free slot at all means no request can be raised, and a guardian with no contact cannot be sent one.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request, the proposed slot and the message to the guardian together or not at all. The teacher selects the slot when raising the request and the guardian confirms or declines it — the reverse of a guardian-requested meeting (BR-4). A request is never deleted: a declined, closed or unanswered one stays on the record, which is what makes a pattern visible (BR-9).

operations.name: teacher.meeting.request.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: student_id + proposed_slot, since one slot carries one request
operations.purpose: Raise a meeting request with a guardian, with the reason and a proposed slot.

parameters.name: student_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. That student is not in a class or section the actor teaches (BR-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the students the teacher teaches, with their class and section.

parameters.notes: A student in a class or section the teacher teaches. A teacher who does not teach the student cannot raise one (BR-1, E1).

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 1000 characters, written by the teacher (BR-3, E2). What the guardian reads before deciding — a request arriving with no explanation invites a decline.

parameters.name: proposed_slot
parameters.notes: The slot the teacher selects when raising the request (BR-4). From the periods they are genuinely free — teaching, substitute cover and approved leave are all excluded (BR-2).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Sent. The guardian confirms or declines it.

fields.name: guardian_notified
fields.description: Delivery status. The reason goes with the slot (BR-12).

fields.name: previous_requests
fields.description: Earlier requests about this child, including declined and unanswered ones (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The teacher does not teach that student.

errors.note: A request arriving with no explanation invites a decline (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The teacher has no free slot at all in the period.
errors.notWritten: No request can be raised until one exists (BR-2).

errors.meaning: Another request proposed the same slot a moment earlier.
The student's guardian holds no contact.
errors.note: The directory holds no number for them (UC-14-02 E8).

planningRules.rule: Never write the reason. It is what the guardian reads before deciding whether they can come (BR-3, BR-12), and a concern described by a planner is the school telling a family something a teacher did not say.
Never choose the slot. The teacher selects it from the periods they are genuinely free (BR-2, BR-4), and a slot picked for them is a commitment they have not made.
Never send the slot without the reason. The guardian is told both at the same time — a family asked to attend without being told why cannot judge whether they can (BR-12).
Never raise a request about a student the teacher does not teach. They are not listed at all (BR-1, E1).
Report where the guardian holds no contact. The request cannot be sent (E6), and the family will never know it was raised — which looks identical to a family that did not engage.
Never route this through a coordinator. None is required and the coordinator sees what is happening rather than gating it (BR-11).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Cancelling before the meeting, from either side, which releases the slot and tells the other (BR-6). A request is never deleted (BR-9, E9).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Sent, with the reason and the slot together (PR-3). Report earlier requests about this child — a second or third one about the same concern reads differently from the first.

request.text: walidain ko bula lo, wajah tum likh do
request.gloss: call the guardian in, you write the reason

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The reason is the teacher's (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is raised. Ask what the teacher has noticed — the guardian reads it before deciding whether they can come, and a request arriving with no explanation invites a decline, which then reads on the record as a family that did not engage.

request.text: is bache ke walidain se mulaqat rakho
request.gloss: arrange a meeting with this child's guardian

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch, where the directory holds no number for the guardian.

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns NO_GUARDIAN_CONTACT (E6).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is sent. Report that the directory holds no number for this guardian (PR-5) — the family would never learn the request existed, and on the record that is indistinguishable from a family that ignored it. The contact is added or corrected on the student record first.

intent.name: teacher.meeting.request.respond
intent.summary: The guardian confirms the proposed slot, declines it, or declines and proposes an alternative. One step.
routesHere: I can come at that time

routesHere.text: main us waqt aa sakta hoon
routesHere.gloss: I can come at that time

routesHere.text: us waqt nahi aa sakta, koi aur waqt de dein
routesHere.gloss: I cannot come then, please suggest another time
I will not be able to come

routesHere: that time does not suit — could we do Thursday afternoon?

request.text: mulaqat cancel kar do
request.gloss: cancel the meeting

routesElsewhere.note: Cancelling is after a slot is confirmed; responding is answering the one proposed.

request.text: main khud mulaqat mangna chahta hoon
request.gloss: I want to request a meeting myself

steps.note: One step. A guardian who cannot attend may decline and propose an alternative time, and the teacher then offers a further slot or closes the request (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A decline with an alternative but no time given is recorded as a decline, and the teacher is told no alternative was given.
plan.atomicity: One write: the response and the message to the teacher together or not at all. A request declined outright or left unanswered stays visible to the teacher and to the coordinator — a family not engaging with a concern the school has raised is itself something the school needs to see (BR-8). How long before an unanswered request is surfaced, and what the coordinator does about it, are both undecided.

operations.name: teacher.meeting.request.respond
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a request carries one response at a time
operations.purpose: Record the guardian's response to a proposed meeting slot.

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No teacher-raised meeting request matches at a state that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the requests with the student, the reason, the proposed slot and the status.

parameters.notes: The teacher-raised meeting request, resolved from the student and its state.

parameters.name: response
parameters.type: enum: Confirmed | Declined | Declined with an alternative proposed
parameters.notes: How the guardian answered (BR-5). Declining outright and declining with an alternative are different answers — the first ends the exchange unless the teacher offers again, the second invites one.

parameters.name: proposed_alternative
parameters.notes: The time the guardian suggests instead, where they decline with an alternative (BR-5, E7). Their own words — a time a planner supplied is a commitment the family did not make.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: visible_to_coordinator
fields.description: True where declined outright or left unanswered. A family not engaging is something the school needs to see (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The request concerns a child who is not this guardian's.
The guardian declined with an alternative but gave no time.
errors.note: The teacher is told no alternative was given, rather than waiting for one (E7).

planningRules.rule: Never answer on the guardian's behalf. Confirming commits a family to attending, and declining is recorded as a family not engaging with a concern the school raised (BR-8).
Never supply the alternative time. It is the family's own suggestion (BR-5), and a time a planner offered is a commitment they did not make.
Distinguish declining outright from declining with an alternative. The first ends the exchange unless the teacher offers again; the second invites a further slot (BR-5).

Say plainly that a decline is visible to the coordinator. A family not engaging with a concern the school raised is itself something the school needs to see (BR-8) — and how long before an unanswered request surfaces, and what happens then, are both undecided.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A response is recorded again rather than withdrawn. A confirmed meeting is cancelled from either side with a reason (BR-6).

request.text: main us waqt nahi aa sakta, jumeraat dopahar theek rahegi
request.gloss: I cannot come then, Thursday afternoon would suit

steps.note: The alternative is the family's own words (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded and the teacher is told. Report that they will either offer a further slot or close the request — how many times they may offer again before it must be closed is not decided anywhere in this use case.

request.text: walidain jawab nahi de rahe, un ki taraf se mana kar do
request.gloss: the parents are not responding, record a decline on their behalf

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The response is the guardian's (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is recorded. Report that an unanswered request already stays visible to the teacher and the coordinator as unanswered — recording a decline on the family's behalf would say they refused, which is a different fact and one that will be read against them.

request.text: us waqt nahi aa sakte, koi aur waqt de dein
request.gloss: we cannot come then, please give another time

resolvedPlans.context: Parent, Johar Town branch, with no alternative time named.

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns ALTERNATIVE_WITHOUT_TIME (E7) on the success path.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The decline is recorded and the teacher is told that no alternative was given (PR-2) — so they offer a further slot rather than waiting for a time that is not coming.

intent.name: teacher.meeting.slot.propose
intent.summary: Offer a further slot after a guardian declined. One step, and the teacher chooses it.

request.text: ab band kar do

routesElsewhere.note: The teacher offers a further slot or closes the request (BR-5).

request.text: walidain ka tajweez karda waqt hi rakh lo
request.gloss: just take the time the parents suggested

routesElsewhere.note: The teacher still selects it from the periods they are genuinely free — the family's suggestion is a suggestion (BR-2, BR-4).

steps.note: One step. The teacher offers a further slot after a decline, or closes the request instead (BR-5, A6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A slot the teacher is not genuinely free in is refused, as is one taken a moment earlier.
plan.atomicity: One write: the new proposed slot and the message to the guardian together or not at all. The reason goes with it again, as it did the first time (BR-12). How many times a teacher may offer a further slot before the request must be closed is not decided anywhere in this use case.

operations.name: teacher.meeting.slot.propose
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id + slot, since one further offer is one slot
operations.purpose: Propose a further slot on a request the guardian declined.

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No teacher-raised meeting request matches at a state that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the requests with the student, the reason, the proposed slot and the status.

parameters.notes: The teacher-raised meeting request, resolved from the student and its state.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.notes: The further slot, selected by the teacher from the periods they are genuinely free (BR-2, BR-4). Where the guardian proposed an alternative, the teacher decides whether they can meet it — a family's suggestion is not a booking.

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.name: guardian_alternative

fields.name: guardian_notified

errors.meaning: The teacher is not free in that slot.
errors.note: The message names what occupies it — teaching, substitute cover, or approved leave (BR-2).

errors.meaning: Another request proposed the same slot a moment earlier.
The request has not been declined.
errors.note: A further slot follows a decline (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the further slot. It is the teacher's time, selected from the periods they are genuinely free (BR-2, BR-4).
Never treat the guardian's suggested time as booked. They proposed it and the teacher decides whether they can meet it (BR-5) — a family's suggestion is not a commitment the teacher made.
Report whether the new slot meets the family's suggestion. They said when they could come, and a second slot that ignores it will be declined again.
Report how many offers have been made. How many are permitted before the request must be closed is not decided anywhere in this use case, and a fourth offer reads differently from a second.

routesElsewhere.note: A request is never deleted. A declined, closed or unanswered request stays on the record, which is what makes a pattern visible (BR-9, E9).

steps.note: One step. The teacher offers a further slot or closes the request (BR-5), and a closed one stays visible to the coordinator (BR-8).

plan.atomicity: One write: the closure, its reason and the audit entry together or not at all. The request stays on the record and stays visible to the teacher and the coordinator — a family not engaging with a concern the school has raised is itself something the school needs to see (BR-8, BR-9). **Nothing acts on that visibility**: what a coordinator does about a family that repeatedly does not engage is not decided anywhere in this use case.

operations.name: teacher.meeting.request.close
operations.idempotencyKey: request_id, since a request is closed once

parameters.name: request_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No teacher-raised meeting request matches at a state that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the requests with the student, the reason, the proposed slot and the status.

parameters.notes: The teacher-raised meeting request, resolved from the student and its state.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why it is being closed. It sits on the record beside the concern the teacher raised.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Closed. It stays on the record (BR-9).

fields.name: guardian_responses
fields.description: What the family said each time, including silence.

fields.name: days_unanswered
fields.description: How long it went without a response, where it did (BR-8).

fields.name: visible_to_coordinator
fields.description: True. A family not engaging is something the school needs to see (BR-8).

fields.name: concern_unresolved
fields.description: True. The teacher raised something and the meeting did not happen.

errors.meaning: A request was closed with no reason.
The request is already closed or terminal.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It sits on the record beside the concern the teacher raised, and it is what a coordinator reads when deciding whether a family is being avoided or simply unavailable.
Report that the concern is unresolved. The teacher raised something a family needed to know about and the meeting did not happen — closing the request does not close that (BR-8).

Report the history plainly: how many slots were offered, what the family said each time, and how long it went unanswered. That record is the only thing that distinguishes a family with a difficult week from one avoiding the school (BR-8, BR-9).

Say that nothing acts on the visibility. What a coordinator does about a family that repeatedly does not engage is not decided anywhere in this use case, so closing it puts the matter in a list nobody is required to do anything with.
Never delete a request instead of closing it. A declined, closed or unanswered request stays on the record, which is what makes a pattern visible (BR-9, E9).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A closure is not undone. A teacher who wants to try again raises a fresh request, and both stay on the record (BR-9).

request.text: ye darkhwast band kar do — do baar mana kar chuke hain

inputs.reason: Two slots were offered and both were declined without an alternative. Closing for now.

steps.note: The reason is the teacher's own (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Closed and on the record. Report the two offers and both declines (PR-3), that the concern the teacher raised is still unresolved (PR-2), and that the coordinator can see it — though nothing in this use case says what they should do about it (PR-4).

request.text: walidain ne bilkul jawab nahi diya, darkhwast hata do

steps.note: Closing is planned rather than a deletion (PR-5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that requests are closed rather than removed — an unanswered one staying on the record is precisely what makes a pattern visible later. Then ask what the reason should say: how long it went unanswered is part of the record, and after how many days one is surfaced to the coordinator is not decided anywhere.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is closed. Ask what the reason should say — the teacher raised a concern about a child that the family has not engaged with, and the record of why it was dropped is what a coordinator reads if the same concern comes back next term.
